title: Crime-Science 'Situational Prevention' Framework for Misuse-Surface Reduction

original_idea.body:
# Crime-Science 'Situational Prevention' Framework for Misuse-Surface Reduction

**Problem:** Crime science's situational crime prevention (reduce opportunity, increase effort/risk of an offense) is a mature design discipline. AI misuse governance argues about capability bans but rarely about systematically reducing the situational opportunity surface.

**Direction:** Transfer the 25-technique situational-prevention taxonomy. Map each technique to a concrete AI-deployment control (rate limits, KYC, monitoring, friction), then audit a sample of public deployment policies for which situational-prevention techniques they actually employ, scoring opportunity-surface coverage.

**Why it matters:** Reframes misuse governance around a proven prevention design discipline and reveals which low-cost situational controls are underused — operationalizing safety into deployment practice. Document analysis only.

**Relevant context:** Situational crime prevention (Clarke, 25 techniques); published deployment/usage policies; misuse-focused frontier safety commitments.
